hook: New algorithms find all long matches across 625 human centromere assemblies with 7.5 times less memory

readout.label: Memory saved vs. state of the art, 625 haplotypes

summary: The authors built TeraMEM, which lists every long exact match between all pairs of genome assemblies using a compressed index of the whole panel. It is also 20 times faster counting index construction. Applied to human centromeres, it flagged large segmental duplications in every chromosome but Y and a ~200 kbp inversion beside the chromosome 2 repeat array. These are preprint results, and the biological findings are descriptive.
title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time
